and You alone:
The right answer is **and You alone**. وَإِيَّاكَ has two parts: وَ means *and*, and إِيَّاكَ means *You alone*, as in إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ, *You alone we worship*, in Al-Fatiha.

Tip: a وَ joined to the front of a word almost always means *and*.
and the mercy:
The right answer is **and the mercy**. وَرَحْمَةُ has two parts: وَ means *and*, and رَحْمَةُ means *mercy*, as in السَّلامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ.

Tip: a وَ joined to the front of a word almost always means *and*.
and with Your praise:
The right answer is **and with Your praise**. وَبِحَمْدِكَ has three parts: وَ *and*, بِ *with*, and حَمْدِكَ *Your praise*.

Tip: a وَ joined to the front of a word almost always means *and*.
is the Greatest:
The right answer is **is the Greatest**. أَكْبَرُ comes from the root ك ب ر, *big*, like كَبِيرٌ, *big*. So اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ is *Allah is the Greatest*.

Tip: a word on the pattern أَفْعَلُ usually means *more* or *most*.
not (of):
The right answer is **not (of)**. غَيْرِ means *other than* or *not*. In Al-Fatiha, غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ is *not (of) those who earned anger*.

Tip: you say it in the opening supplication too: وَلا إِلٰهَ غَيْرُكَ, *there is no god other than You*.
